expl.summary: Each jet is placed on 16 neurons, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each class score adds some neurons and subtracts others; this smaller formula, tuned in step 2 towards the network's decision for each jet, reaches an accuracy of 64.1% on the validation set. The t score is built from size: it subtracts neuron 13 (ΣzΔR below 0.148 and λ₁+λ₂ below 0.0146, -38%), on which tops sit far below every other class, and adds neuron 10 (λ₁+λ₂ and mass/pT, +29%), so it follows λ₁+λ₂, ΣzΔR² and ΣzΔR with rank correlations of about 0.9. The q score adds neuron 9 (narrow, centred jets below 53.3 GeV, +38%) and neuron 6 (+17%) and subtracts neuron 10 (-22%) and neuron 4 (-11%). The g score adds neuron 2 (low subjet-pair mass and little Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½, +30%), neuron 1 (+17%) and neuron 9 (+14%), and subtracts neuron 5 (pT held by the few hardest particles, -20%), on which quarks sit highest. The W and Z scores share the positive input from neuron 7 (a two-prong jet with mass/pT between 0.0795 and 0.0906) and the negative inputs from neurons 6 and 3; the W score adds in addition neuron 11 (compact, centred, elongated jets, +27%) and neuron 0, while W and Z are separated by neuron 14 (mass/pT between 0.0798 and 0.0889 with subjets more than 0.159 apart), which the Z score adds (+7%) and the W score subtracts (-10%). Freezing neuron 14 costs 4.84 accuracy points, more than any other neuron.

0.title: compact jet with its three subjet axes 0.105-0.307 apart
0.measures: Pushed up for compact jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.013, 20% of its input) whose largest distance between the three subjet axes lies between 0.105 and 0.307 (max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.105 and < 0.307, about 15% each); pushed down for the very narrowest jets (ΣzΔR < 0.0788, λ₁ < 0.00477), for light jets (mass < 62.5 GeV) and, more weakly, for subjet distances above 0.179 and 0.231. It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ and falls with planar flow (rank correlations 0.46 and -0.46). The mean is 4.01 for W, 3.87 for Z, 1.93 for q, 1.16 for g and 1.01 for t; it is zero for 64.6% of tops and 26.8% of gluons, but only for 3.6% of W and 4.6% of Z jets.
0.role: It raises the W score (+12%) and lowers the g score (-9%). It does not enter the q, Z or t scores.

1.title: light jets with pT reaching the 7th and 8th particles
1.measures: Pushed up for small ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² (< 0.00385), light jets (mass < 50.6 GeV), ΣzΔR < 0.0774 and high total pT (log of total pT > 6.6), each about 7-11% of its input; pushed down for the narrowest jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.00992), small mass/pT (< 0.0623) and a soft 8th-hardest particle (z₇ < 0.0625). It rises with the pT of the 7th and 8th particles (pT₆, pT₇, rank correlations 0.527 and 0.581) and falls with the pT share of the 5 hardest particles (-0.513). The mean is 2.97 for g, 1.72 for Z, 1.42 for t, 1.40 for q and 1.39 for W; it is zero for 6.6% of gluons and for 21-33% of the other classes.
1.role: It raises the g score (+17%) and the Z score (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: low subjet-pair mass, small angularity, moderate total pT
2.measures: Pushed down for large angularity (Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.132, its strongest term, -12%) and for a soft 8th-hardest particle (pT₇ < 54.1 GeV); pushed up for a largest subjet-pair mass below 62.4 GeV, λ₁ < 0.00599 and total pT below 820 GeV (log of total pT < 6.57). It rises with M₂ and z₇ (rank correlations 0.552 and 0.53) and falls with the largest subjet-pair mass (-0.488). The mean is 6.15 for g, 3.20 for q, 1.98 for t, 1.88 for W and 1.59 for Z; it is zero for 12.3% of gluons, 41.1% of quarks and 54-60% of W and Z jets.
2.role: It raises the g score (+30%), where it is the largest input. It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores.

3.title: wide jets with two subjets more than 0.185 apart
3.measures: Pushed up for λ₁+λ₂ > 0.00549 (21% of its input), two subjet axes more than 0.185 apart (ΔR(2 subjets) > 0.185), ΣzΔR > 0.0874 and a three-subjet distance above 0.186; pushed back down for the widest jets (λ₁+λ₂ > 0.0138, -15%) and ΣzΔR² > 0.00895. It follows λ₁+λ₂, λ₁ and the pT share and number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlations 0.596, 0.594, 0.589 and 0.582). The mean is 5.96 for t, 1.48 for g, 0.71 for q, 0.57 for Z and 0.05 for W; it is zero for 96.2% of W jets, 88.4% of quarks, 76% of gluons, 60.9% of Z jets and 20% of tops.
3.role: It lowers the W score (-12%) and the Z score (-19%), and raises the t score only slightly (+2%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

4.title: λ₁+λ₂ with small e₃ and subjets within 0.374
4.measures: Switched down for narrow jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.00896, -26%, its strongest term), for jets whose farthest particle is within 0.179 (max ΔRᵢ < 0.179) and for a small minor axis (λ₂ < 0.000586); pushed up for small e₃ (< 0.000149, +22%) and a three-subjet distance below 0.374 (+19%). It rises with λ₁+λ₂, ΣzΔR, λ₁ and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlations 0.77-0.79). The mean is 4.23 for t, 3.84 for Z, 2.79 for W, 1.85 for g and 1.06 for q; it is rarely zero (17.3% of quarks, 6.9% of gluons, 1.5-2.6% of the others).
4.role: It raises the Z score (+4%) and the t score (+6%), and lowers the q score (-11%) and the g score (-2%). It does not enter the W score.

5.title: pT held by the few hardest particles, very narrow core
5.measures: Pushed up for a soft 8th-hardest particle (z₇ < 0.0744, 17% of its input, with further steps at z₇ < 0.0486 and < 0.026), for very narrow, centred jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.00154 with centroid offset < 0.0251, λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00337, about 12% each) and for 5 hardest particles above 489 GeV with a soft 7th particle (pT₆ < 49.6 GeV); pushed down when the hardest particle sits very close to the axis (z₀ΔR₀ < 0.0214). It rises with the summed pT of the 3 hardest particles (rank correlation 0.748) and falls with z₇ (-0.743). The mean is 10.63 for q, 3.93 for g, 3.60 for W, 3.28 for Z and 0.82 for t; it is zero for 55% of tops and 9.1% of quarks. Its values reach about 30.
5.role: It raises the q score (+9%) and lowers the g score (-20%) and the t score (-21%). It does not enter the W or Z scores.

6.title: light jets with λ₁ below 0.00724 but ΣzΔR² above 0.00919
6.measures: Its two strongest terms pull in opposite directions: λ₁ < 0.00724 pushes it up (+22.5%) and ΣzΔR² < 0.00919 pushes it down (-26%), so it is largest for jets with a small principal axis that are not among the most compact. Smaller terms push it up for τ₁ < 0.128 with small mean φ² spread, two subjets closer than 0.18, ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² < 0.00292 and a soft 7th particle at moderate total pT. It falls with jet mass and the largest subjet-pair mass (rank correlations -0.703 and -0.694). The mean is 5.83 for q, 4.93 for g, 1.87 for t, 1.54 for W and 1.20 for Z; it is zero for 55.9% of Z jets and 5% of quarks. It reproduces the network's own neuron poorly (correlation 0.035).
6.role: It raises the q score (+17%) and the g score (+8%), and lowers the W score (-13%) and the Z score (-22%). It does not enter the t score.

7.title: elongated two-prong jet with mass/pT between 0.0795 and 0.0906
7.measures: Built from many size steps: pushed down for ΣzΔR² above 0.00673 and 0.00438 and for ΣzΔR < 0.0894, pushed up for λ₁+λ₂ > 0.00863; pushed up for mass/pT > 0.0795 (+7%) and down again above 0.0906 (-7.5%), so it peaks in that mass/pT window; pushed up for two subjets closer than 0.157 and down below 0.186. It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ and falls with planar flow, D₂ and τ₂₁ (rank correlations 0.55, -0.55, -0.452 and -0.416). The mean is 6.93 for Z, 5.60 for W, 2.88 for g, 1.99 for t and 1.50 for q; it is zero for 59.7% of tops and 56.5% of quarks but for only about 5% of W and Z jets.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+34%), where it is the largest input, and the W score (+12%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

8.title: narrow, centred jets with a small minor axis
8.measures: Pushed up for λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00355 (+29%), for ΣzΔR² < 0.00696 with centroid offset < 0.0288 and for mass < 48.6 GeV with λ₂ < 0.000168; pushed down for the very narrowest jets (ΣzΔR < 0.0572 with ΣzΔR² < 0.00478, -29%) and for very light jets (mass < 21.5 GeV with λ₂ < 0.000241). It falls with λ₁+λ₂, ΣzΔR and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlations about -0.59). The mean is 1.38 for q, 0.94 for g, 0.30 for W, 0.17 for Z and 0.08 for t; it is zero for 92.9% of tops, 83.7% of Z jets and 49.1% of gluons.
8.role: It enters only two class scores and only weakly: it raises the t score (+2%) and lowers the W score (-2%). It does not enter the g, q or Z scores.

9.title: narrow, centred jets below 53.3 GeV
9.measures: Pushed up for ΣzΔR² < 0.0059 (29% of its input), for mass < 53.3 GeV with centroid offset < 0.0258, for centroid offset < 0.018 and for three subjet axes within 0.226; pushed down for very light jets (mass < 27.8 GeV). It falls with λ₁+λ₂, λ₁, ΣzΔR and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlations -0.763 to -0.74). The mean is 6.49 for q, 5.12 for g, 3.30 for W, 1.69 for Z and 0.67 for t; it is zero for 84.7% of tops, 53.6% of Z jets and 12.9% of quarks.
9.role: It raises the q score (+38%), where it is the largest input, and the g score (+14%); it lowers the Z score slightly (-2%). It does not enter the W or t scores.

10.title: λ₁+λ₂ and mass/pT, wide in both axes
10.measures: Pushed down for a small principal axis (λ₁ < 0.00552, -14%), a soft 8th-hardest particle (z₇ < 0.0667) and ΣzΔR² < 0.00289; pushed up for a large minor axis (λ₂ > 0.000307, +11%), pT₇ < 45.2 GeV and λ₁ > 0.00752. It follows λ₁+λ₂, ΣzΔR² and λ₁ (rank correlations 0.912, 0.912 and 0.907) and mass/pT (0.879). The mean is 9.56 for t, 3.80 for Z, 3.31 for W, 2.57 for g and 1.29 for q; it is zero for 39.5% of quarks, 10.3% of gluons and 0.4% of tops. Its values reach about 24.
10.role: It raises the t score (+29%) and lowers the q score (-22%). It does not enter the g, W or Z scores.

11.title: compact, centred, elongated jets with subjets 0.173-0.26 apart
11.measures: Pushed up for ΣzΔR² < 0.0128 (30% of its input) and centroid offset < 0.0407 (+15%), for z₇ > 0.0176, a three-subjet distance below 0.26 and planar flow < 0.281; pushed down for the very narrowest jets (ΣzΔR < 0.0718) and for three-subjet distances below 0.173. It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ and falls with planar flow, D₂ and τ₂₁ (rank correlations 0.543, -0.543, -0.492 and -0.468). The mean is 8.78 for W, 7.50 for Z, 4.00 for g, 2.58 for q and 2.13 for t; it is zero for 58.6% of tops, 43.9% of quarks and about 3% of W and Z jets.
11.role: It raises the W score (+27%), where it is the largest input. It does not enter the g, q, Z or t scores.

12.title: very wide, massive jets with particles beyond ΔR 0.4
12.measures: Almost always zero: it needs ΣzΔR² > 0.0189 (+34%), mass > 60.7 GeV with an off-centre pT centroid, mass > 82.7 GeV or centroid offset > 0.0454, and is pushed down for ΣzΔR² > 0.0139 and for a hardest particle far from the axis (z₀ΔR₀ > 0.0398). It follows the number of particles at ΔR ≥ 0.4 (rank correlation 0.783). It is non-zero for 30.7% of tops and at most 6.2% of the other classes; the mean is 0.45 for t, 0.14 for g, 0.05 for q and 0.00 for W and Z.
